biography.plain_text: Daniel Chávez Morán is a Mexican hotel developer and founder of Grupo Vidanta. Trained as a civil engineer, he built a resort business around vacation-club memberships, with brands including Mayan Palace and Grand Luxxe. The group combines accommodation with golf and entertainment. He later stepped back from daily operations while developing partnerships.

long_biography.plain_text:
Before entering tourism, Vidanta founder Daniel Chávez Morán built basketball courts under a government programme serving poor communities. He used his contracting profits to finance his first hotel. The resulting Paraíso Mazatlán project opened in 1974, followed by another hotel in the same city.

His mother, Delia Morán, was a teacher whose work inspired the foundation he established in her name. Supported by Grupo Vidanta, its educational centre serves children from low-income families in Nayarit. Alongside tutoring and computer classes, it offers music, dance and sports. The centre also provides meals and counselling, while San Javier Hospital donates its medical services.
